name: hangup
description:
gvmd hangs up rather than replying when it rejects a command: a live gvmd 25.2.1 closes the socket immediately after answering a pre-authenticate command, and the next send fails with a broken pipe. This scenario points that behaviour at the importer's response framer -- the connection dies with no bytes delivered.

THIS SCENARIO ASSERTS A DEFECT, DELIBERATELY. gmp_read_element is written as if recv_until returns an empty value at EOF:

    tok = conn.recv_until(b">", ...)
    if len(str(tok)) == 0:
        return None, "connection closed before a complete response was read"

The runtime does not do that. recv_until RAISES at EOF, so the run dies with 'failed to call main function: recv_until: EOF' and that error branch is unreachable dead code. A mid-run hangup therefore aborts the whole import with an opaque runtime error instead of the intended message -- and because gvmd really does hang up, this is reachable in production.

The assertion below pins today's wrong behaviour so the gap stays visible. When gmp_read_element is fixed to survive EOF, this scenario will fail: replace the log_contains entry with 'connection closed before a complete response was read' at that point.
